$comment: THE list of API keys the board knows about — read by the server (server/secrets.mjs: only these names can be saved), the board's API keys dialog (src/lib/apiKeys.ts) and tests/test_api_keys.py (every key must be read by something). Values are stored beside it in setup/.env (git-ignored, docker-ignored, never served). Each key has a kind: secret (masked; the default), url (shown in full), email or text (shown in full). 'planned: true' marks a key the user can add now that nothing reads yet; tests/test_api_keys.py exempts only those. Services are shown grouped (groups[], in order) and alphabetically by name inside a group; 'why' is the one-line summary (≤ 44 chars, so it never truncates), 'details' the full explanation shown when a row is opened. Service colours are soft and never red or red-orange (red means a rejected key; a test enforces it).

services.name: Jira
services.getIt: Jira → Profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.jiraBase from the config.

services.details: Pulls every ticket on the board. Without it nothing can be fetched.

services.name: Atlassian Cloud
usedBy: Bitbucket (when no HTTP access token is set)
services.getIt: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token

keys.label: Account email
keys.hint: Cloud API calls sign in with this email plus the token.

keys.label: Site URL
keys.hint: Your Cloud site, e.g. https://your-org.atlassian.net — not id.atlassian.com (that is where tokens are made).

services.details: One API token for Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket on Atlassian Cloud, as they move off on-prem.

services.name: Bitbucket
services.getIt: Bitbucket → Personal settings → HTTP access tokens (read scope is enough)

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.bitbucketBase from the config.

services.details: Adds real branches, pull requests and review state to the cards.

services.name: Confluence
services.why: Linked pages for the agent fallback
services.getIt: Confluence → Profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.confluenceBase from the config.

services.details: Lets the agent fallback read linked Confluence pages. The normal fetch does not need it.

services.name: Jenkins
services.getIt: Jenkins → your name → Configure → API Token → Add new token

keys.label: Jenkins URL
keys.hint: e.g. https://jenkins.example.com — lets Test check your user and token. Builds still come from the job links in jenkins.jobs.

keys.label: Projects folder
keys.hint: The folder that holds your projects, e.g. https://jenkins.example.com/job/portfolios/ — the board finds each repository's pipelines (build and deploy, per environment) under it. Without it only the job links in jenkins.jobs are used.

keys.label: API token
keys.hint: Explicit job links per repository and environment (jenkins.jobs) are optional and override what discovery finds.

services.details: Reads the latest build of a ticket's branch per environment and pipeline: result, tests, deploy target, failed stage. Pipelines are found under the projects folder; run python3 jira-intern/jenkins.py discover <repo> to see what it finds.

services.name: Checkmarx One
services.getIt: Checkmarx One → Identity and Access Management → API Keys (the Checkmarx MCP server uses the same key)

keys.label: Tenant API URL
keys.hint: e.g. https://your-tenant.cxone.cloud — or endpoints.checkmarxBase in the config.

keys.label: Token URL
keys.hint: Only when the IAM host differs from the API host.

services.details: Confirms which vulnerabilities a fix ticket actually closed, for its PR readiness report.

services.name: Dynatrace
services.why: Evidence from linked traces and problems
services.getIt: Dynatrace → Access tokens (Account Management → Identity & access → Platform tokens) with the read scopes storage:spans:read, storage:events:read, storage:logs:read, storage:buckets:read

keys.label: Tenants
keys.hint: Environment name = tenant id, comma separated, e.g. prod=abc12345,uat=def67890 — the id is the first part of your Dynatrace address. Only links to these tenants are ever read. Also accepted: endpoints.dynatraceTenants in the config; this setting wins.

services.details: Read-only. Reads the Dynatrace links on a ticket (a trace, a problem, a log search) and nothing else: for a trace id it asks for that trace's spans, for a problem the Davis problem, for a log link its error logs. Only tenants listed here are ever contacted, so a link to any other host is ignored. Test sends one small query per tenant.

services.name: Claude
services.details: Runs Cloud AI with Claude models, billed to this key's Anthropic account.

services.name: Cursor
services.details: Runs Cloud AI with Cursor models, and the default agent fallback when the fast fetch fails.

services.name: Gemini
services.details: Runs Cloud AI with Gemini models, billed to this key's Google account.

services.name: OpenAI
services.details: Only for the agent fallback when the codex connector is the active one.

services.name: GitHub
services.getIt: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens (fine-grained, read-only)
services.details: Not used yet — for repositories hosted on GitHub.
